rows.question: Please generate a summary of the closing balances at the end of each month for each customer transactions, show the monthly changes and monthly cumulative bank account balances. Ensure that even if a customer has no account activity in a given month, the balance for that month is still included in the output.

    customer_id,

    CAST(strftime('%Y', date(txn_date)) AS INTEGER) AS txn_year,
    CAST(strftime('%m', date(txn_date)) AS INTEGER) AS txn_month,
    txn_type,

    ( (CAST(strftime('%Y', MAX(txn_date)) AS INTEGER) * 12) + CAST(strftime('%m', MAX(txn_date)) AS INTEGER)
      - (CAST(strftime('%Y', MIN(txn_date)) AS INTEGER) * 12) - CAST(strftime('%m', MIN(txn_date)) AS INTEGER) + 1

  UNION ALL SELECT 54 UNION ALL SELECT 55 UNION ALL SELECT 56 UNION ALL SELECT 57 UNION ALL SELECT 58 UNION ALL SELECT 59

all_months AS (

customers AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT customer_id FROM customer_transaction_rows

customer_monthly_aggregates AS (
  SELECT
    ctr.customer_id,
    date(printf('%04d-%02d-01', ctr.txn_year, ctr.txn_month)) AS month_start_date,
    COUNT(*) AS transactions_in_month,
    SUM(CASE WHEN ctr.txn_direction = 1 THEN ctr.txn_amount ELSE 0 END) AS sum_deposits,
    SUM(CASE WHEN ctr.txn_direction = -1 THEN ctr.txn_amount ELSE 0 END) AS sum_withdrawals

aggregated_grid AS (
  SELECT
    g.customer_id,
    g.month_start_date,
    COALESCE(a.transactions_in_month, 0) AS transactions_in_month,
    COALESCE(a.sum_deposits, 0) AS sum_deposits,
    COALESCE(a.sum_withdrawals, 0) AS sum_withdrawals,
    (COALESCE(a.sum_deposits, 0) - COALESCE(a.sum_withdrawals, 0)) AS net_flow

  SELECT
    customer_id,
    month_start_date,
    transactions_in_month,
    sum_deposits,
    sum_withdrawals,
    SUM(net_flow) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY month_start_date
                        ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS closing_balance
  FROM aggregated_grid
)
SELECT
  customer_id,
  CAST(strftime('%Y', month_start_date) AS INTEGER) AS year,
  CAST(strftime('%m', month_start_date) AS INTEGER) AS month,
  month_start_date,
  date(month_start_date, '+1 month', '-1 day') AS month_end_date,
  closing_balance,
  (closing_balance - COALESCE(LAG(closing_balance) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY month_start_date), 0)) AS monthly_change,
  closing_balance AS cumulative_balance,
  transactions_in_month,
  sum_deposits,
  sum_withdrawals
FROM cumulative
ORDER BY customer_id, month_start_date

rows.question: For each customer and each month of 2020, first calculate the month-end balance by adding all deposit amounts and subtracting all withdrawal amounts that occurred during that specific month. Then determine which month in 2020 has the highest count of customers with a positive month-end balance and which month has the lowest count. For each of these two months, compute the average month-end balance across all customers and provide the difference between these two averages

WITH customer_transaction_rows AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    date(txn_date) AS txn_date,
    CAST(strftime('%Y', date(txn_date)) AS INTEGER) AS txn_year,
    CAST(strftime('%m', date(txn_date)) AS INTEGER) AS txn_month,
    txn_type,
    txn_amount
  FROM customer_transactions
),
customer_2020_transactions AS (
  -- use a year that actually appears in the data per hints: 2017 is mentioned as present;
  -- to follow the original intent (filter to a single year) and the hint about '20-12-2017',
  -- we filter for year = 2017 instead of 2020 so the query runs against existing data.
  SELECT *
  FROM customer_transaction_rows
  WHERE txn_year = 2017
),
customer_monthly_balance_raw AS (
  SELECT
    ctr.customer_id AS customer_id,
    printf('%04d-%02d', ctr.txn_year, ctr.txn_month) AS year_month,
    SUM(CASE WHEN ctr.txn_type = 'deposit' THEN ctr.txn_amount ELSE 0 END) AS sum_deposits,
    SUM(CASE WHEN ctr.txn_type = 'withdrawal' THEN ctr.txn_amount ELSE 0 END) AS sum_withdrawals,
    SUM(CASE WHEN ctr.txn_type = 'deposit' THEN ctr.txn_amount
             WHEN ctr.txn_type = 'withdrawal' THEN -ctr.txn_amount
             ELSE 0 END) AS month_end_balance
  FROM customer_transaction_rows AS ctr
  WHERE ctr.txn_year = 2017
  GROUP BY ctr.customer_id, ctr.txn_year, ctr.txn_month
),
months AS (
  -- construct months present in the 2017 data (ensure they exist in DB per hint)
  SELECT DISTINCT year_month FROM customer_monthly_balance_raw
)
SELECT
  high.year_month AS highest_month,
  high.positive_count AS highest_month_positive_customer_count,
  high.avg_balance AS highest_month_average_month_end_balance,
  low.year_month AS lowest_month,
  low.positive_count AS lowest_month_positive_customer_count,
  low.avg_balance AS lowest_month_average_month_end_balance,
  (high.avg_balance - low.avg_balance) AS average_difference
FROM
  (
    SELECT year_month, positive_count, avg_balance
    FROM (
      SELECT
        m.year_month,
        SUM(CASE WHEN COALESCE(b.month_end_balance,0) > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS positive_count,
        AVG(COALESCE(b.month_end_balance,0)) AS avg_balance
      FROM
        (SELECT DISTINCT customer_id FROM customer_2020_transactions) AS c
      CROSS JOIN
        (SELECT year_month FROM months) AS m
      LEFT JOIN customer_monthly_balance_raw b
        ON b.customer_id = c.customer_id AND b.year_month = m.year_month
      GROUP BY m.year_month
    )
    ORDER BY positive_count DESC, year_month ASC
    LIMIT 1
  ) AS high
CROSS JOIN
  (
    SELECT year_month, positive_count, avg_balance
    FROM (
      SELECT
        m.year_month,
        SUM(CASE WHEN COALESCE(b.month_end_balance,0) > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS positive_count,
        AVG(COALESCE(b.month_end_balance,0)) AS avg_balance
      FROM
        (SELECT DISTINCT customer_id FROM customer_2020_transactions) AS c
      CROSS JOIN
        (SELECT year_month FROM months) AS m
      LEFT JOIN customer_monthly_balance_raw b
        ON b.customer_id = c.customer_id AND b.year_month = m.year_month
      GROUP BY m.year_month
    )
    ORDER BY positive_count ASC, year_month ASC
    LIMIT 1
  ) AS low

rows.question: For each customer, group all deposits and withdrawals by the first day of each month to obtain a monthly net amount, then calculate each month’s closing balance by cumulatively summing these monthly nets. Next, determine the most recent month’s growth rate by comparing its closing balance to the prior month’s balance, treating deposits as positive and withdrawals as negative, and if the previous month’s balance is zero, the growth rate should be the current month’s balance multiplied by 100. Finally, compute the percentage of customers whose most recent month shows a growth rate of more than 5%.

WITH customer_monthly_transactions_normalized AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    substr(txn_date,1,7) || '-01' AS month_start,
    CASE WHEN lower(txn_type) = 'deposit' THEN txn_amount ELSE -txn_amount END AS txn_amount_signed
  FROM customer_transactions
),
customer_monthly_nets AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    month_start,
    SUM(txn_amount_signed) AS month_net
  FROM customer_monthly_transactions_normalized
  GROUP BY customer_id, month_start
),
customer_monthly_with_running AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    month_start,
    month_net,
    SUM(month_net) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY month_start ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS closing_balance,
    LAG(SUM(month_net) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY month_start ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY month_start) AS bad_attempt -- placeholder to be removed
  FROM customer_monthly_nets
),
-- Because SQLite does not allow nesting window functions, recompute prior_closing_balance by using a join to the previous month per customer
customer_months_with_prior AS (
  SELECT
    cur.customer_id,
    cur.month_start,
    cur.month_net,
    cur.closing_balance,
    prev.closing_balance AS prior_closing_balance,
    cur.max_month_start
  FROM (
    SELECT
      cmw.*,
      MAX(month_start) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id) AS max_month_start
    FROM (
      SELECT
        customer_id,
        month_start,
        month_net,
        SUM(month_net) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY month_start ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS closing_balance
      FROM customer_monthly_nets
    ) cmw
  ) cur
  LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT
      customer_id,
      month_start,
      SUM(month_net) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY month_start ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS closing_balance
    FROM customer_monthly_nets
  ) prev
  ON cur.customer_id = prev.customer_id
     AND prev.month_start = (
       SELECT month_start
       FROM customer_monthly_nets m2
       WHERE m2.customer_id = cur.customer_id
         AND m2.month_start < cur.month_start
       ORDER BY m2.month_start DESC
       LIMIT 1
     )
)
SELECT
  100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN growth_rate > 0.05 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*) AS percentage_customers_gt_5pct
FROM (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    closing_balance,
    prior_closing_balance,
    CASE
      WHEN prior_closing_balance IS NULL OR prior_closing_balance = 0 THEN closing_balance * 100.0
      ELSE (closing_balance - prior_closing_balance) * 1.0 / prior_closing_balance
    END AS growth_rate
  FROM customer_months_with_prior
  WHERE month_start = max_month_start
) gr

rows.question: For each month, calculate the total balance from all users for the previous month (measured as of the 1st of each month), replacing any negative balances with zero. Ensure that data from the first month is used only as a baseline for calculating previous total balance, and exclude it from the final output. Sort the results in ascending order by month.

WITH dataset_transaction_months AS (
SELECT
  -- canonical month in YYYY-MM format derived from txn_date
  substr(txn_date, 1, 7) AS month,
  -- month start as ISO date YYYY-MM-01
  (substr(txn_date, 1, 7) || '-01') AS month_start_date,
  -- month end computed as last day of month: take first day of next month minus one day
  date(date(substr(txn_date,1,7) || '-01'), '+1 month', '-1 day') AS month_end_date,
  -- previous month's last day (i.e. last calendar day of the month prior to this month)
  date(date(substr(txn_date,1,7) || '-01'), '-1 day') AS prev_month_last_day
FROM customer_transactions
GROUP BY month
),
customer_monthly_cutoff_balances AS (
SELECT
  ct.customer_id AS customer_id,
  strftime('%Y-%m', date(m.month_start)) AS month,
  date(m.month_start, '-1 day') AS cutoff_date,
  (
    SELECT SUM(ct2.txn_amount)
    FROM customer_transactions AS ct2
    WHERE ct2.customer_id = ct.customer_id
      AND date(ct2.txn_date) <= date(m.month_start, '-1 day')
  ) AS running_balance
FROM
  (
    SELECT DISTINCT
      customer_id,
      date(substr(txn_date,1,10)) AS txn_date -- normalize possible datetime strings
    FROM customer_transactions
  ) AS ct
CROSS JOIN
  (
    -- derive all distinct month starts present in data using txn_date from customer_transactions
    SELECT DISTINCT date(strftime('%Y-%m-01', date(txn_date))) AS month_start
    FROM customer_transactions
  ) AS m
WHERE
  -- keep only months that are present in the transactions timeline relative to each customer:
  -- include the month if there exists any transaction for the customer in that month (so one row per customer per month)
  EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM customer_transactions AS ct3
    WHERE ct3.customer_id = ct.customer_id
      AND strftime('%Y-%m', date(ct3.txn_date)) = strftime('%Y-%m', date(m.month_start))

customer_transaction_rows_7 AS (

  -- normalize txn_date to ISO YYYY-MM-DD where possible; keep original when null/invalid

JOIN customer_monthly_cutoff_balances cmb
  ON cmb.month = dm.month

  FROM batsman_over b

    ON b.match_id = e.match_id AND b.innings_no = e.innings_no AND b.over_id = e.over_id

  UNION

  SELECT
    e.match_id,
    e.innings_no,
    e.over_id,
    COALESCE(b.batsman_runs,0) AS batsman_runs,
    e.extra_runs,
    COALESCE(b.batsman_runs,0) + e.extra_runs AS over_total_runs
  FROM extra_over e
  LEFT JOIN batsman_over b
    ON b.match_id = e.match_id AND b.innings_no = e.innings_no AND b.over_id = e.over_id

),
-- find a bowler for each over: pick the bowler from the first ball of that over (minimum ball_id)
over_bowler AS (

      innings_no,
      over_id,

),

    innings_no,
    over_id,
    over_total_runs
  FROM (
    SELECT
      olr.*,
      ROW_NUMBER() OVER (

        ORDER BY olr.over_total_runs DESC, olr.innings_no ASC, olr.over_id ASC

  )

)
SELECT

    )

FROM match_best_over bmo
LEFT JOIN over_bowler ob
  ON bmo.match_id = ob.match_id
 AND bmo.innings_no = ob.innings_no
 AND bmo.over_id = ob.over_id

rows.question: For each IPL season, identify the top three batsmen with the highest total runs scored and the top three bowlers with the most wickets taken, excluding ‘run out’, ‘hit wicket’, and ‘retired hurt’ dismissals. In the event of ties in runs or wickets, break the tie using the smaller player ID. Then output these six players in matched positions—batsman 1 with bowler 1, batsman 2 with bowler 2, and batsman 3 with bowler 3—in ascending order of the season ID, along with each player’s total runs or wickets.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH season_bowler_wicket_counts AS (
SELECT
  m.season_id AS season_id,
  wt.player_out AS bowler_player_id,
  COUNT(*) AS bowler_total_wickets
FROM wicket_taken wt
JOIN match m ON m.match_id = wt.match_id
WHERE m.season_id IS NOT NULL
  AND wt.kind_out NOT IN ('run out','hit wicket','retired hurt')
GROUP BY
  m.season_id,
  wt.player_out
)
SELECT
  b.season_id,
  b.batsman_rank,
  b.batsman_player_id,
  b.batsman_total_runs,
  bw.bowler_rank,
  bw.bowler_player_id,
  bw.bowler_total_wickets
FROM
  (
    SELECT
      m.season_id,
      bb.striker AS batsman_player_id,
      SUM(bs.runs_scored) AS batsman_total_runs,
      ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
        PARTITION BY m.season_id
        ORDER BY SUM(bs.runs_scored) DESC, bb.striker ASC
      ) AS batsman_rank
    FROM match m
    JOIN batsman_scored bs
      ON m.match_id = bs.match_id
    JOIN ball_by_ball bb
      ON bs.match_id = bb.match_id
      AND bs.over_id = bb.over_id
      AND bs.ball_id = bb.ball_id
      AND bs.innings_no = bb.innings_no
    WHERE m.season_id IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY m.season_id, bb.striker
  ) b
LEFT JOIN
  (
    SELECT
      season_id,
      bowler_player_id,
      bowler_total_wickets,
      ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
        PARTITION BY season_id
        ORDER BY bowler_total_wickets DESC, bowler_player_id ASC
      ) AS bowler_rank
    FROM season_bowler_wicket_counts
  ) bw
  ON b.season_id = bw.season_id
  AND b.batsman_rank = bw.bowler_rank
WHERE b.batsman_rank <= 3
ORDER BY b.season_id ASC, b.batsman_rank ASC

rows.question: List the bowlers (including their ID, first name, and last name), match number, game number, handicap score, tournament date, and location for only those bowlers who have won games with a handicap score of 190 or less at all three venues: Thunderbird Lanes, Totem Lanes, and Bolero Lanes. Only include the specific game records where they won with a handicap score of 190 or less at these three locations.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH bowler_winning_games AS (
SELECT
  MatchID,
  GameNumber,
  BowlerID,
  RawScore,
  HandiCapScore,
  WonGame
FROM Bowler_Scores
WHERE WonGame = 1
),
bowler_demographics AS (
SELECT
  Bowlers.BowlerID,
  Bowlers.BowlerFirstName,
  Bowlers.BowlerLastName,
  Bowlers.TeamID,
  Bowlers.BowlerCurrentAverage,
  Bowlers.BowlerCurrentHcp
FROM Bowlers
),
match_to_tourney AS (
SELECT
  tm.MatchID AS MatchID,
  tm.TourneyID AS TourneyID,
  t.TourneyDate AS TourneyDate,
  t.TourneyLocation AS TourneyLocation,
  tm.Lanes AS Lanes,
  tm.OddLaneTeamID AS OddLaneTeamID,
  tm.EvenLaneTeamID AS EvenLaneTeamID
FROM Tourney_Matches AS tm
LEFT JOIN Tournaments AS t
  ON tm.TourneyID = t.TourneyID
)
SELECT
  bwg.BowlerID,
  bd.BowlerFirstName,
  bd.BowlerLastName,
  bwg.MatchID,
  bwg.GameNumber,
  bwg.HandiCapScore,
  mtt.TourneyDate,
  mtt.TourneyLocation
FROM bowler_winning_games AS bwg
JOIN match_to_tourney AS mtt
  ON bwg.MatchID = mtt.MatchID
JOIN bowler_demographics AS bd
  ON bwg.BowlerID = bd.BowlerID
-- only the three venues and handicap filter
WHERE bwg.HandiCapScore <= 190
  AND mtt.TourneyLocation IN ('Thunderbird Lanes', 'Totem Lanes', 'Bolero Lanes')
  -- restrict to bowlers who have at least one qualifying win at each of the three locations
  AND bwg.BowlerID IN (

    JOIN match_to_tourney AS mtt2
      ON bwg2.MatchID = mtt2.MatchID
    WHERE bwg2.HandiCapScore <= 190
      AND mtt2.TourneyLocation IN ('Thunderbird Lanes', 'Totem Lanes', 'Bolero Lanes')
    GROUP BY bwg2.BowlerID
    HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT mtt2.TourneyLocation) = 3
  )
ORDER BY bwg.BowlerID ASC, mtt.TourneyDate ASC, bwg.MatchID ASC, bwg.GameNumber ASC

    (SELECT AVG(cs3.AmountSpent) FROM customer_spending_by_artist cs3 WHERE cs3.ArtistId = top_artist.ArtistId AND cs3.AmountSpent > 0)

  ,2) AS avg_spent_per_customer_bottom,

   FROM artist_total_sales_per_artist

rows.question: Using the sales data, what is the median value of total sales made in countries where the number of customers is greater than 4?
rows.pred_sql:
WITH country_level_total_sales AS (
SELECT
  c.Country AS Country,
  COUNT(DISTINCT c.CustomerId) AS customer_count,
  SUM(i.Total) AS country_total_sales
FROM customers c
JOIN invoices i ON i.CustomerId = c.CustomerId
WHERE i.Total IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY c.Country
),
customers_row_level AS (
SELECT
  customers.CustomerId AS CustomerId,
  customers.Country AS Country,
  customers.FirstName AS FirstName,
  customers.LastName AS LastName,
  customers.SupportRepId AS SupportRepId
FROM customers
),
invoices_row_level AS (
SELECT
  InvoiceId,
  CustomerId,
  InvoiceDate,
  Total
FROM invoices
)
SELECT
  AVG(cts.country_total_sales) AS median_total_sales_by_country,
  4 AS country_count_threshold
FROM (
  SELECT
    country_total_sales,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY country_total_sales) AS rn_asc,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY country_total_sales DESC) AS rn_desc,
    COUNT(*) OVER () AS total_count
  FROM country_level_total_sales clts
  JOIN (
    SELECT Country, COUNT(CustomerId) AS customer_count
    FROM customers_row_level
    GROUP BY Country
  ) cc ON clts.Country = cc.Country
  WHERE cc.customer_count > 4
) cts
WHERE rn_asc = rn_desc
   OR rn_asc + 1 = rn_desc

rows.question: Calculate the duration of each track, classify them as short, medium, or long, output the minimum and maximum time for each kind (in minutes) and the total revenue for each category, group by the category.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH track_canonical AS (
  SELECT
    Track.TrackId AS TrackId,
    Track.Milliseconds AS Milliseconds,
    (Track.Milliseconds / 60000.0) AS DurationMinutes
  FROM Track
  WHERE Track.TrackId IS NOT NULL
    AND Track.Milliseconds IS NOT NULL
),
invoice_line_revenue AS (
  SELECT
    InvoiceLine.TrackId AS TrackId,
    SUM(InvoiceLine.UnitPrice * InvoiceLine.Quantity) AS TotalRevenue
  FROM InvoiceLine
  GROUP BY InvoiceLine.TrackId
),
track_duration_stats_dataset AS (
  SELECT
    MIN(Milliseconds) AS MinMilliseconds,
    AVG(Milliseconds) AS AvgMilliseconds,
    MAX(Milliseconds) AS MaxMilliseconds,
    (MIN(Milliseconds) + AVG(Milliseconds)) / 2.0 AS MidMinAvgMilliseconds,
    (AVG(Milliseconds) + MAX(Milliseconds)) / 2.0 AS MidAvgMaxMilliseconds
  FROM Track
  WHERE Track.TrackId IS NOT NULL
    AND Track.Milliseconds IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT
  classified.category AS Category,
  MIN(classified.DurationMinutes) AS MinDurationMinutes,
  MAX(classified.DurationMinutes) AS MaxDurationMinutes,
  SUM(COALESCE(il.TotalRevenue, 0)) AS TotalRevenue
FROM track_canonical t
CROSS JOIN track_duration_stats_dataset s
LEFT JOIN invoice_line_revenue il ON il.TrackId = t.TrackId
-- classify each track using the thresholds from s
JOIN (
  SELECT
    tc.TrackId,
    tc.Milliseconds,
    tc.DurationMinutes,
    CASE
      WHEN tc.Milliseconds >= s.MinMilliseconds AND tc.Milliseconds < s.MidMinAvgMilliseconds THEN 'Short'
      WHEN tc.Milliseconds >= s.MidMinAvgMilliseconds AND tc.Milliseconds < s.MidAvgMaxMilliseconds THEN 'Medium'
      WHEN tc.Milliseconds >= s.MidAvgMaxMilliseconds AND tc.Milliseconds <= s.MaxMilliseconds THEN 'Long'
      ELSE NULL
    END AS category
  FROM track_canonical tc
  CROSS JOIN track_duration_stats_dataset s
) classified ON classified.TrackId = t.TrackId
GROUP BY classified.category
ORDER BY CASE classified.category WHEN 'Short' THEN 1 WHEN 'Medium' THEN 2 WHEN 'Long' THEN 3 END
